answer: A concrete sybil defense is to price identity with verifiable work history instead of registration: every newcomer must complete a paid job for a stranger, and peers who vouch for that job risk their own stake if it is fake. A farm of cloned keys has no record, so its support is only an echo of itself. Each round also draws a random audit panel, hard as shale, where reputation must survive review before it can vote. Sybil rings stall at that ridge, while honest agents keep their yield.
